Subject: Voucher conversion — possibility to convert accelerator vouchers into dedicated credit?

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Solstice is excited. We have a stack of accelerator vouchers (outlined in the attached spreadsheet) and a fast follow-on conversation with one of our investors who wants us to move onto a paid, predictable plan.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood convert or exchange these accelerator vouchers into a discount against a Dedicated capacity commitment?
- If yes, what does activation and invoicing look like (timeline, paperwork, and any minimum term implications)?

We'd like to avoid a short-term dedicated commitment if possible; ideally vouchers would translate into one-time credit or a structured top-up to a monthly committed pool. Marcus (CC) suggested exploring a revenue-share or milestone-backed swap as an alternative to a straight discount.

Attached: solstice_voucher_summary.xlsx (counts by voucher, expiration).

Appreciate a quick sense of feasibility — we have an internal deadline to decide by next Friday.

Best,
Anna
Founder & CEO
Solstice AI

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Voucher conversion — possibility to convert accelerator vouchers into dedicated credit?

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the voucher summary. Quick answer up front: yes, we can usually structure a conversion path, but the mechanics depend on (1) voucher terms (expiry/transferability), (2) desired commercial outcome (one-time credit vs ongoing committed pool), and (3) accounting/tax treatment for your investor.

Ben — can you confirm: what's our standard playbook for voucher-to-dedicated exchanges (both one-time credit and staggered conversion)? Also, any restrictions we should flag (e.g., vouchers issued under promotions that disallow conversion)?

Laura — can you pull the standard term sheet for a small Dedicated monthly commit (6/12 month) and flag whether we support milestone-backed payment schedules? I'll draft two options for Anna:

Option A — Voucher-for-Credit: Convert voucher value to a one-off credit applied to the first invoice for Dedicated. No change to standard term length, credit is consumed before billing.

Option B — Voucher-as-Commitment Top-up: Vouchers are counted against committed minimum in month 1 and converted into a time-bound committed pool (we'd propose a 3-month ramp window). This preserves predictable capacity but requires an executed amendment.

I'll follow up with timelines and a sample term sheet in a separate note.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive — Startups
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Anna Morales <anna@solstice.ai>, Marcus Chen <marcus@seedvc.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voucher conversion — possibility to convert accelerator vouchers into dedicated credit?

Olga / Anna — overview from Sales Ops & Pricing:

1) Voucher eligibility: If vouchers were issued by Redwood marketing and are transferable, we can reclassify their USD-equivalent value subject to program rules. If vouchers were promotional with a strict use-only clause, we may need legal sign-off — Laura, flag if any voucher IDs look restricted.

2) Accounting box: For one-off credits we treat them as contra-revenue on the earliest invoice (no change to committed term). For a committed pool conversion we need an executed amendment (modifies both invoicing and revenue recognition). That has implications for trial/billing dates.

3) Examples/precedents: I ran a similar exchange in Q1 where we applied ~$50k worth of vouchers as a 3-month committed pool; activation took 7 business days once paperwork signed.

4) If Marcus is proposing a milestone-backed swap (e.g., incremental credits released as Solstice hits MRR milestones), we can support it but it requires a simple Performance Addendum (payment and release triggers). That typically adds 3–4 business days for legal review.

Next steps I recommend:
- Olga: send a short SOW/term proposal with both Option A and B and a suggested timeline (we can mirror the Q1 precedent).
- Laura: attach the 6/12 month term sheets and a redline marker for the Performance Addendum.

Ben
Head of Startup GTM
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Vouchers are transferable and expire Jan 31, 2028. Total face value is ~$38k (details in attachment).
- Prefer Option B (top-up to committed pool) if we can get a short ramp and the ability to scale down after month 3 if we miss MRR targets — investor is wary of long locks.
- Marcus prefers the milestone-release structure on the first $15k to reduce investor cash exposure.

Can you sketch an activation timeline that gets us to a signed amendment and live Dedicated capacity before Oct 1? That would let us start load testing.

Best,
Anna

Anna / Marcus — thanks. Proposed activation plan below to hit your Oct 1 target: 

Day 0 (Today): We confirm voucher serials and transferability (solstice_voucher_summary.xlsx) — Ben/Laura already have these.
Day 1: We issue a 1-page Commercial Addendum capturing Option B with a 3-month ramp and milestone-release clause for the first $15k (Performance Addendum draft).
Day 2–3: Solstice signs the addendum; Redwood signs (expedited signature via DocuSign).
Day 4: Finance issues pro forma invoice reflecting committed pool (vouchers applied as committed credit).
Day 5–7: DevOps schedules Dedicated pool activation (we can provision a small starter pool within 48 hours of Finance confirmation; full quota available by Day 7).

Conditions & notes:
- If you want the 3-month ramp to include an automatic scale-down clause, we'll include a usage review at 90 days and allow a single-step reduction in committed capacity with 30 days' notice. That will affect pricing tiers slightly (I'll include specifics).
- Legal: Laura to circulate the redlines for the Performance Addendum; expect a 2–4 business day review window.

I'm attaching the draft term sheet and will route the 1-page addendum for signature as soon as you confirm. If we're aligned, I'll queue the DocuSign this afternoon so we can hit the Oct 1 activation.

Cheers,
Olga
